mostWorthwhile.text: Following fat from intestinal cells into chylomicrons and then lymph was most worthwhile: the planned pictures and prose distinguish its initial route from the blood route of glucose and amino acids.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate glucose and amino-acid crossings were clear but repetitive, and neither explained the transport mechanism across the intestinal cell.

surprise.text: I expected the fat and packaging materials to combine directly, but packaging required the villus hotspot. The result also explained that cells rebuild fat before packaging it into chylomicrons.

arbitrary.text: Using the villus again for both packaging and lacteal entry felt like a station requirement rather than an obvious biological necessity, although the compatibility feedback resolved both attempts.

continue.text: I would continue: comparing the nutrient routes was useful, and I would be curious to see what happens after they reach the liver and bloodstream. The repeated hotspot requirement was a minor friction.
